findings.source_quote: ὁ τρυφῶν καὶ ἀπατώμενος μίαν ἡμέραν καὶ πράσσων ἃ βούλεται
findings.english_quote: A person who takes pleasure and is deceived for even one day, doing whatever he wants
findings.issue: “Even” adds scalar emphasis to the duration that is not expressed in the selected clause. The Greek specifies one day without this intensifier, and current project policy prohibits added intensifiers.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove “even”: “A person who takes pleasure and is deceived for one day, doing whatever he wants”. This proposed replacement requires fresh review before adoption.

summary: Both editions were independently checked against every clause of the supplied working source. The standard edition has no concrete fidelity defect identified; the simplified edition needs one minor correction for added emphasis. Both preserve the difficult assertions about saving pleasures, securing life, and procuring death, including the condition of persistence without repentance. “Servants” and contextual “repent” follow current policy. The bracketed φησί tags are editorial supplements; their omission does not remove preserved speech content or change speaker attribution. The repentance note is editorial explanation, not translated source text. These judgments concern the supplied text and disclosures only, not authentication of unseen editions, manuscript images, or exhaustive collation.
